facts.statement: Protoplotus is an extinct genus of waterbirds that lived in Indonesia during the early to mid-Cenozoic, likely in the Eocene.
facts.quote: Protoplotus (meaning "original Plotus") is an extinct genus of waterbird that inhabited Indonesia during the early-mid Cenozoic, most likely during the Eocene.

facts.statement: The genus contains only one species, P. beauforti, known from a largely complete and well-preserved skeleton found in the Sangkarewang Formation of Indonesia.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, P. beauforti (named after Lieven Ferdinand de Beaufort) known from a largely complete, well-preserved skeleton from the Sangkarewang Formation of Indonesia.

facts.statement: Protoplotus was a small waterbird that lived in a freshwater rift lake where the Sangkarewang Formation was deposited.
facts.quote: Protoplotus was a rather small waterbird that inhabited the freshwater rift lake where the Sangkarewang Formation would be deposited.

facts.statement: Protoplotus resembled modern cormorants and darters in appearance and lifestyle, and was once thought to belong to the Anhingidae family.
facts.quote: It closely resembled and likely had a similar lifestyle to modern cormorants and darters, and for a while was considered to belong to the Anhingidae.

facts.statement: Recent studies show Protoplotus is distinct from cormorants and darters, placing it in its own family, Protoplotidae, which is related to both groups.
facts.quote: However, more recent studies have found it to be distinct from both, and it is now placed in its own family, which is thought to be related to both cormorants and anhingas.

facts.statement: Protoplotus lived from the Danian to the Priabonian stages, between 66 and 33.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Danian to Priabonian (66 to 33.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Protoplotus belongs to the family Protoplotidae.
The genus Protoplotus was described by Lambrecht in 1931.

rejected.statement: The single known fossil skeleton of Protoplotus uniquely preserves gastroliths, suggesting the animal may have seasonally switched its diet from fish to fruit.
rejected.quote: Uniquely, the single fossil skeleton of Protoplotus preserves gastroliths. This suggests that it may have seasonally switched its diet from fish to fruit.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'may have seasonally switched its diet from fish'

rejected.statement: Protoplotus is classified within the class Aves.
